WhisperManager.description: Creates a scheduled one-off whisper task for a slot account.
WhisperManager.detail: Creates a delayed message tied to an account. When the command is called from an AI or assistant slot, the current slot account can be used without passing `accountId`. It does not start a relay session; it only adds a whisper record that will be injected into the matching account flow when its time arrives.

AIAIChatStart.description: Starts a continuous relay session between AI1 and AI2.
AIAIChatStart.detail: Opens a sequential, ongoing relay flow between the AI1 and AI2 slots. Both AI slots must already be connected. The starter parameter selects which AI produces the first message, and the app sends either the `analyze-AI1-AI2` or `analyze-AI2-AI1` protocol accordingly. This is for starting a session, not for sending a one-off message.

AIAIChatStop.description: Stops the active AI-AI relay session.
AIAIChatStop.detail: Ends the running AI1 ↔ AI2 relay flow. The app sends the `[STOP][ANALYZE][AI-AI]` control protocol to the two AI slots and stops automatic forwarding.

AIAssistantChatStart.description: Starts a continuous relay session between the selected AI slot and the assistant.
AIAssistantChatStart.detail: Opens a back-and-forth relay flow between the selected AI slot and ai0. The source AI and the assistant must already be connected. At startup, the selected AI receives the `AI-assistant` protocol. Use this command for a session, not for a one-off handoff.

AIAssistantChatStop.description: Stops the active AI-assistant relay session.
AIAssistantChatStop.detail: Ends the running assistant relay flow. The app sends the `[STOP][ANALYZE][AI-ASSISTANT]` control protocol to the related source slot.

SlotBridge.description: Runs the canonical slot command bus.
SlotBridge.detail: Collects cross-slot messaging, waited replies, attachment delivery, `connection.ensure`, `session.open`, `session.switch`, `session.sync`, and `room.command` dispatch inside one JSON envelope. This is the only supported command surface for new slot and room integrations.
SlotBridge.usage:
++cmd:SlotBridge({"action":"message.send","fromSlot":"ai1","toSlot":"ai0","payload":{"text":"Hello"}})
Actions: message.send, message.sendWait, connection.ensure, session.open, session.switch, session.sync, room.command

• No extra params → read the full file
• head=N → read the first N lines
• tail=N → read the last N lines

⚠️ For explicit ranges, always use start_line + end_line together. head/tail are meant to be used on their own.

• head=60 → first 60 lines
• tail=20 → last 20 lines
• start_line=100, end_line=200 → lines 100-200

write.description:
Write content to a file. Creates a new file or overwrites an existing one when overwrite=true.

⚠️ SIZE LIMIT: Do not use this tool if the content exceeds 500 lines or roughly 50KB.
Large payloads can become incomplete or malformed because of LLM output token limits.

🔄 FOR LARGE FILES: Use the hev_fs_start_chunked_session → hev_fs_write_chunk → hev_fs_finalize_chunked flow.
That flow provides UTF-8 validation, checksum support, and rollback protection.
write.overwrite: Overwrite the existing file if present (default: false)
write.agentGuidance: Use this when you need to create a file or replace it completely. For files larger than 500 lines / 50KB, use hev_fs_start_chunked_session instead. Use hev_fs_edit for partial changes. Be careful with overwrite=true.

edit.description:
Apply pattern-based edits to a file.

USAGE: edits: [{old_text: 'existing text', new_text: 'new text'}]
old_text is matched exactly in the file and replaced with new_text.

PARAMETERS:
• edits (required): array of {old_text, new_text}. At least one edit is required.
• dry_run: preview only when true, apply changes when false (default: false)
• all_or_nothing: if true, no edits are applied when any single edit fails (default: false)
• match_scope: 'first'|'last'|'all'|[0,2] — choose which occurrences change (default: 'all')
• ignore_whitespace: ignore whitespace differences while preserving original formatting (default: false)
• normalize_eol: 'lf'|'crlf'|'auto'|'preserve' — end-of-line normalization (default: 'auto')

IMPORTANT:
• old_text must match the file content exactly (including indent and newlines)
• use match_scope when there are multiple occurrences
• use all_or_nothing=true for critical edits
• test with dry_run=true before applying changes
edit.edits: Edit list. Each item is {old_text: string, new_text: string}. old_text is the text to replace and new_text is the replacement value.
edit.dryRun: true: preview only, false: apply changes
edit.allOrNothing: true: roll back all edits if any edit fails. false: keep successful edits
edit.matchScopeEnum: first: first match, last: last match, all: all matches
edit.ignoreWhitespace: true: ignore whitespace/indent differences and preserve formatting. false: exact match
edit.normalizeEol: Line endings: lf (Unix), crlf (Windows), auto (preserve file style), preserve (do not change)
edit.agentGuidance: Use this for partial file edits instead of rewriting the full file. Test with dry_run=true first, then apply with dry_run=false. old_text must match exactly. Use match_scope='first' when only the first occurrence should change. Use all_or_nothing=true for critical edits. Run hev_dev_check_syntax after edits to .ts/.tsx files.
